messages:
leo: Heads up — after the fw tighten last night about 15% of eu-gpu nodes are stuck in 'joining'. bootstrap logs show KMS decrypt failures when the keystore agent hits privatelink.

carrie: I pulled a couple logs from the failing nodes:
```
2026-03-21T02:14:03Z keystore[pid=42] ERROR: kms:DecryptAccessDenied: access denied for key arn:aws:kms:eu:12345:key/abcd
2026-03-21T02:14:03Z bootstrap[info] failed to fetch keystore: decrypt failed
```

kevin: Seems like the new default-deny egress rule (fw-ephem-2026) blocked the privatelink endpoint used for KMS/keystore. The rule was scoped to subnets with tag:gpu-join.

leo: Oof. @sre-oncall can we do a scoped rollback? I know it's annoying from an audit perspective but this is blocking capacity.

sre-oncall: I prefer a scoped short rollback rather than global. Proposal: add an exception for outbound to kms-vpce-10-2-3-4:443 from subnets with tag gpu-join for 30 minutes, collect flowlogs/pcap, then re-tighten. Also capture an audit marker in the incident tracker.

deploy-bot: Canary saw 3 node join attempts fail and auto-backfill kicked in. If we leave this, other regions will try to pick up load -> cost + latency.

ashley: Quick cost note: backfilling from us-west and apac did a temporary bump last 3 hours — rough estimate +$2.5k/day if this continues. Rolling back for 30m and letting warm pools finish is cheaper than sustained cross-region backfill.

carrie: Agreed. Steps I'm going to run:
1) open fw exception (scoped to ip 10.2.3.4/32 port 443 for gpu-join subnets)
2) restart keystore agent on joining nodes (`systemctl restart keystore-agent`)
3) watch join rate and keystore logs for decrypt success
4) capture flowlogs and mark audit note + PR in infra-audit repo to record temporary exception

kevin: Commands for rollback (I'll raise the quick terraform change after):
```
# quick allow in security group (temporary)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0gpujoin --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.2.3.4/32 --description "temp keystore allow for gpu join"
# restart agent on nodes (run via fleet-run)
fleetctl run --filter 'tag:subnet=gpu-join and state:joining' 'systemctl restart keystore-agent'
```

carrie: I'll also attach the flowlog query we want to store in the audit ticket: `fields srcaddr, dstaddr, action | filter dstaddr==10.2.3.4 and dstport==443`

leo: Sounds good. Please @me when rolled back. Also let's not forget to follow up with an IAM change so the keystore role can use the privatelink principal (avoids needing rollback next time).

sre-oncall: Noted. We'll capture the time window in audit, include evidence, and then close the exception.

carrie: Rolled back at 1768019920. Kicking restarts now.

deploy-bot: Auto-backfill noticed capacity improving, throttles backing off.

carrie: Keystore logs on previously stuck nodes now show decrypt success:
```
2026-03-21T02:26:58Z keystore[pid=42] INFO: Decrypt succeeded for node-id i-0aa1
2026-03-21T02:27:01Z bootstrap[info] node joined cluster: i-0aa1
```

ashley: Initial cost check: we avoided cross-region backfill; estimated cost delta for the hour ~ $120. Good call.

kevin: I'll open a terraform PR to add the VPC endpoint allow rule with documented IAM condition and a test canary to exercise join flow in staging. PR: infra/terraform#3721

leo: Great — leave the exception open for 30m from rollback then re-tighten and verify. Thanks team :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Monitoring until 1768020100, will re-tighten then and post results.
